The DS06-102-DUT-LF is a lead-free pressure reducing valve from Resideo (Honeywell Home), 1 inch, NPT connection, double union.

A pressure reducing valve sits where the water service enters the building and holds house pressure at a set value regardless of what the street is doing. Municipal mains commonly run well above what residential fixtures are rated for, and street pressure is not constant — it climbs at night when demand drops.

Uncontrolled pressure is what shortens the life of everything downstream. Fill valves, supply lines, washing machine hoses and water heaters all fail earlier on high pressure, and most plumbing codes cap what may be delivered to fixtures. The PRV is the single component that decides whether the rest of the system lives at its rated pressure.

This is a DialSet valve: the outlet pressure is set on a dial on the valve itself, without plumbing in a gauge and without trial and error. On a commissioning visit that is the difference between setting the pressure in a minute and chasing it with a test gauge and an adjusting screw.

The double union body comes apart on both sides, so the valve is removed and serviced without cutting the line. On a water service that is often the only accessible point in the system, that matters more than it sounds.

Lead free construction, as required for potable water in the United States.

Size the valve to the service line, not to the fixture count. An oversized PRV hunts at low flow; an undersized one starves the building at peak draw.

The VR8345M4302 is a gas control valve from Resideo (Honeywell Home) for universal appliances.

The gas valve is the component that admits fuel to the burner and shuts it off. It carries the main shutoff, the pressure regulator that holds manifold pressure steady as supply pressure varies, and the safety interlock that keeps gas off until the control system has proved it is safe to light.

This is a universal valve, built to serve intermittent pilot and direct ignition systems both. One part number covers applications that would otherwise take two, which is why it is the valve a service truck carries.

Gas appliance safety. A gas valve must match the appliance it is fitted to — ignition system, capacity, inlet pressure and gas type. Replacement is work for a licensed gas technician, and the appliance manufacturer's parts list is what decides the correct valve, not the physical fit of the threads. If the replacement does not match, the appliance can fail to light, fail to prove flame, or overfire.

Water heater tempering kit from Resideo (Honeywell Home), part number AMX300TLF/U: DirectConnect mixing valve, tee and 8 inch flex connector in one package.

A mixing valve solves a problem that has no other answer: a water heater has to be kept hot enough to suppress bacterial growth in the tank, and that temperature is too hot to deliver to a tap. The valve blends stored hot water with cold on its way out, so the tank stays hot and the fixture does not.

Beyond safety, tempering buys capacity. A tank held hot and blended down delivers considerably more usable hot water than the same tank set to delivery temperature, because each gallon drawn is stretched with cold.

Lead free construction, as required for potable water in the United States.

Set the outlet temperature with a thermometer at the fixture, not by the dial alone, and re-check it after the system has settled. Inlet conditions move the mix, and a valve set on a cold line reads differently once the loop is up to temperature.

The L4006H1004 is a control from Resideo (Honeywell Home) that senses boiler water temperature and switches the burner, the circulator, or both. It operates over a 100–240 °F range.

The aquastat is the control that keeps a hydronic boiler inside its working band. It holds the water hot enough to serve a call for heat and shuts the burner down before the boiler reaches a temperature the relief valve would have to handle.

This is a manual reset high limit. Once it trips, the control stays open until someone presses the button — the boiler does not simply restart when the water cools. That is deliberate: a high limit trip means something went wrong upstream, and a self-resetting limit would hide it.

This model ships without an immersion well. If you are replacing a control whose well is still sound, reuse it; if you are starting from a bare tapping, order a well to match.

A factory stop at 240 °F caps the adjustment so the high limit cannot be set past the point the boiler is rated for.

When you replace an aquastat, match the temperature range, the switch action and the differential to the control coming out, not to the boiler nameplate. A boiler will happily run on a control with the wrong range — it will simply cycle badly, or trip a limit that was never meant to be the working control.

The sensing bulb belongs in an immersion well, filled with heat conductive compound, threaded into the tapping the boiler manufacturer provided for it. A bulb strapped to the outside of a pipe reads the pipe, not the water, and it reads it late.

The UMV500-LF is a lead-free thermostatic mixing valve from Resideo (Honeywell Home), 3/8 inch.

A mixing valve solves a problem that has no other answer: a water heater has to be kept hot enough to suppress bacterial growth in the tank, and that temperature is too hot to deliver to a tap. The valve blends stored hot water with cold on its way out, so the tank stays hot and the fixture does not.

Beyond safety, tempering buys capacity. A tank held hot and blended down delivers considerably more usable hot water than the same tank set to delivery temperature, because each gallon drawn is stretched with cold.

This valve mounts under the sink and serves three- or four-port arrangements, tempering at the fixture where the run from the heater is long enough that whole-house blending alone leaves the tap too hot or too slow.

Lead free construction, as required for potable water in the United States.

The flame sensor is the appliance's proof that the burner is actually lit. A flame conducts current in one direction only, and the control measures that rectified microamp signal. No signal, no gas — the valve closes within seconds.

Most "furnace lights then shuts down" calls end here. Oxide builds on the rod over seasons and chokes a signal that is measured in millionths of an amp. Cleaning buys time; a rod that has thinned or warped needs replacing.

Position is as important as condition. The rod has to sit in the flame envelope through the whole firing range, not just at light-off, and a burner that has been re-shaped by years of service can leave a perfectly good sensor sitting in the wrong place.

The L6006A1145 is a control from Resideo (Honeywell Home) that senses boiler water temperature and switches the burner, the circulator, or both. It operates over a 100–240 °F range, with SPDT contacts.

The 3 in capillary lets the sensing bulb sit in the boiler while the control body mounts where it can be reached and wired.

When you replace an aquastat, match the temperature range, the switch action and the differential to the control coming out, not to the boiler nameplate. The L4006E1117 is a controller from Resideo (Honeywell Home) that senses boiler water temperature and switches the burner, the circulator, or both. It operates over a 100–240 °F range, with SPST contacts.

The aquastat is the control that keeps a hydronic boiler inside its working band. It holds the water hot enough to serve a call for heat and shuts the burner down before the boiler reaches a temperature the relief valve would have to handle.

This is a manual reset high limit. Once it trips, the control stays open until someone presses the button — the boiler does not simply restart when the water cools. That is deliberate: a high limit trip means something went wrong upstream, and a self-resetting limit would hide it.

As a high limit, this control has one job that matters more than the rest: it stops the burner before the boiler gets away. Everything else in the heating system is comfort; the high limit is safety.

When you replace an aquastat, match the temperature range, the switch action and the differential to the control coming out, not to the boiler nameplate. A boiler will happily run on a control with the wrong range — it will simply cycle badly, or trip a limit that was never meant to be the working control.

The sensing bulb belongs in an immersion well, filled with heat conductive compound, threaded into the tapping the boiler manufacturer provided for it. A bulb strapped to the outside of a pipe reads the pipe, not the water, and it reads it late.
